title: Decision metadata index and differential hop metrics
creator: Sophie Martinez
description:
Problem: As requests traverse smart routing (region selection, tier routing, fallback to model variants) we currently produce per-hop raw logs that are bulky and hard to query for longitudinal analysis. Engineers and SREs need fast answers to questions like: why did a request failover to a lower tier in eu-west-1? how much latency was introduced by each decision hop? which policy changed the routing for requests from particular customers?

Goal: Build a lightweight, queryable decision metadata index and a compact 'differential hop metrics' stream that captures per-hop deltas (latency, token-count, cost-estimate delta, decision-reason) rather than full payloads. The index should allow fast retrieval by request_id, customer_id, and model_variant, and support retrospective playback and SLO attribution without retaining verbose per-hop artifacts indefinitely.
acceptance_criteria: A compact decision index (Parquet/ORC) is generated and populated for every completed request with fields: request_id, trace_id, customer_id, final_model_variant, first_region, final_region, route_tier_sequence (encoded), total_latency_ms, created_at
A differential hop metrics stream (Kafka topic) emits per-hop records containing hop_index, request_id, delta_latency_ms, delta_kv_entries, cost_delta_estimate, decision_reason_code, sampling_flag
API endpoint /internal/decisions/{request_id} returns aggregated index row within 200ms for 99th percentile of test queries (dataset size ~30M rows), with RBAC enforcement
Retention policy: raw verbose hop artifacts can be tiered to cold storage; index + differential stream retained hot for 90 days and compacted daily
End-to-end tracing correlation maintained: index rows include trace_id and span_ids for at least first and last hop
Query examples in the Console: region-change-freq dashboard and per-customer fallback-rate chart are powered by this index and match baseline SQL validation tests
design_notes: Index design uses columnar files partitioned by date and customer_id prefix to support high-cardinality customers without tiny files
Differential hop metrics intentionally omit sensitive request payloads; decision_reason_code is an enumerated string (eg 'tier_throttled','region_unavailable','fallback_quantized')
We prefer an append-only Kafka topic with compaction key (request_id, hop_index) and a downstream Flink job to compute final aggregates and write index files to S3
Sampling strategy: full capture for high-severity incidents via an incident flag; otherwise probabilistic reservoir sampling with per-customer adjustable quota; sampling_flag propagates to index

Cost model: emitting differential deltas reduces average record size by ~6x compared to full per-hop envelope, estimated infra cost savings ~40% on storage and egress when combined with daily compaction
Compatibility: binary schema evolution considered; use Protobuf with a stable v1 and a documented migration plan for v2 fields
implementation_plan: Schema PR: add Protobuf v1 schema for differential_hop and decision_index (ENG-PR-3782) - owner @arjun
Kafka topic provision and retention tuning (dev/stage/prod) - infra task created

Flink job: read raw hop events, compute deltas per hop, enrich with metadata (customer tier, region), emit to differential topic and write aggregates to staging parquet - initial implementation in rust-flink connector
Index writer: daily compaction Spark/Trino job that merges staging parquet into partitioned index with transactional commits
Console integration: new API route /internal/decisions/{request_id} that reads index (hot store) and falls back to compaction view for late-arriving data
Feature flags: rollout behind feature flag 'decision_index_v1' with canary on 5% of traffic, then 25% before full rollout
Security review: ensure decision_reason_code and customer_id are allowed in logs; mask PII per policy
storage_schema: Index columns: request_id, trace_id, customer_id, customer_tier, first_region, final_region, model_path_sequence (string), route_tier_sequence (string), total_latency_ms, total_token_count, cost_estimate_cents, sampling_flag, created_at, completed_at
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): enable index for internal dev services only and validate schema stability and consumer read paths
Phase 1 (5%): enable differential hop metrics emission behind flag for 5% prod traffic; monitor topic lag, index write throughput, and storage growth
Phase 2 (25%): expand to 25% while running cost/regression checks and populating Console dashboards in read-only mode
Phase 3 (full): flip flag for all routing stacks and begin retention policy enforcement and cold storage tiering
Rollback: disable emission and revert to previous tracing snapshot if Kafka lag or index write error rate > 5% for 10m
qa_checks: Integration tests that replay synthetic routing traces and assert differential delta sums equal full-hop totals
Load test: verify index writes sustain 10k writes/s with <5s compaction lag in staging
Security: automated scan validates no request prompt/response payload fields are present in differential messages
Cross-check: Console dashboards must produce identical fallback-rate numbers to existing baseline queries within 0.5%
SLO: /internal/decisions/{request_id} p99 < 200ms for 95% of synthetic query workload
